s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of unilateral facial and limb weakness with impaired motor function
salient_findings: Incomplete closure of the right eye
Flattening of the right nasolabial fold
key_facts: 66-year-old man
24-hour history of symptoms
3-year history of hypertension
No history of neurological disorders
Alert and oriented
Effacement of the right frontal wrinkle
Incomplete closure of the right eyelid
Muscle strength in the right upper and lower extremities: grade 0/5
Hemorrhage in the left thalamus-radiation crown region and in the lateral ventricle on CT scan
No definitive lesions in the brainstem on cerebral MRI
Corticobulbar tract appeared thinner on the left side than on the right on diffusion tensor imaging

shortlist.label: Ischemic stroke
shortlist.why_kept: Acute onset of unilateral facial and limb weakness with impaired motor function, despite hemorrhage on CT scan, ischemic stroke cannot be ruled out due to potential for hemorrhagic transformation

shortlist.label: Intracerebral hemorrhage
shortlist.why_kept: Hemorrhage in the left thalamus-radiation crown region and in the lateral ventricle on CT scan, consistent with intracerebral hemorrhage

shortlist.label: Cerebral amyloid angiopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Hemorrhage on CT scan, and patient's age, raise concern for cerebral amyloid angiopathy

shortlist.label: Hypertensive encephalopathy
shortlist.why_kept: 3-year history of hypertension, and acute onset of symptoms, suggest possible hypertensive encephalopathy

shortlist.label: Arteriovenous malformation
shortlist.why_kept: Hemorrhage on CT scan, and lack of other clear explanations, make arteriovenous malformation a plausible consideration

raw.rationale: The patient's CT scan shows hemorrhage in the left thalamus-radiation crown region and in the lateral ventricle, which is consistent with intracerebral hemorrhage. The patient's symptoms, such as incomplete closure of the right eye, flattening of the right nasolabial fold, and right-sided hemiplegia, are also consistent with a left-sided intracerebral hemorrhage.

rejected.label: Ischemic stroke
rejected.why: The CT scan shows hemorrhage, not ischemia, which is more consistent with intracerebral hemorrhage than ischemic stroke

rejected.label: Cerebral amyloid angiopathy
rejected.why: There is no evidence of amyloid angiopathy on the imaging studies, and the patient's age and symptoms are more consistent with hypertensive intracerebral hemorrhage

rejected.label: Hypertensive encephalopathy
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and imaging findings are more consistent with a focal lesion, such as intracerebral hemorrhage, rather than a diffuse process like hypertensive encephalopathy

rejected.label: Arteriovenous malformation
rejected.why: There is no evidence of an arteriovenous malformation on the imaging studies, and the patient's symptoms and history are more consistent with a spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage
